en: A rainbow appears when sunlight refracts and reflects inside spherical raindrops, separating white light into its component colors.
Mayon Volcano's slopes feature highly fertile volcanic soil because erupted ash continuously adds essential plant nutrients like potassium.
Pumice is a lightweight volcanic rock that floats on water because it contains numerous trapped gas bubbles from rapid cooling.
Morning fog in Baguio forms when warm, moist air cools below its dew point, causing water vapor to condense into tiny liquid droplets.
Shadows cast by the Sun at noon in the Philippines point north because the Sun is directly overhead or slightly to the south.
The three aligned stars of Orion's Belt are visible in the Philippine night sky from December to February, helping farmers track seasons.
During a full moon, the combined gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun creates higher high tides along Manila Bay.
A storm surge pushes massive amounts of seawater inland during a typhoon, causing severe coastal flooding in areas like Tacloban.
The amihan or northeast monsoon brings cool, dry air to the Philippines between November and February, creating a distinct dry season.
Deforestation on steep slopes accelerates soil erosion because tree roots no longer hold the dirt together during heavy monsoon rains.
Stalactites in Puerto Princesa Subterranean River grow slowly over thousands of years as mineral-rich water drips and deposits calcium carbonate.
You see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels through the air much faster than sound waves do.
